name: GUATEMALA
lead: Guatemala is in Central America. Smoking volcanoes tower over Maya temples. Cloud forests drip with mist. Mild highland weather gives it the nickname Land of Eternal Spring. People speak 22 Mayan languages here every day.
geo: Guatemala has 37 volcanoes. Three are still active. The highlands stay cool all year. Rainforest covers the northern Petén lowlands, where howler monkeys and jaguars live.
Lake Atitlán fills an ancient volcanic crater, ringed by three more volcanoes. In the east, a short Caribbean coast has warm beaches and coral reefs.
animals: The resplendent quetzal is Guatemala's national bird. Its tail feathers grow up to 65 cm and shimmer green and red. The ancient Maya used them as money.
Jaguars still roam the Petén jungle, alongside tapirs, scarlet macaws and harpy eagles. Sea turtles nest on Pacific beaches between July and November.
culture: Maya people make up about 40% of Guatemalans. Women weave cloth called huipiles on backstrap looms. Each village has its own pattern.
Chichicastenango market fills a town square twice a week with flowers, textiles and incense. Marimba, a giant wooden xylophone, makes the national sound.
history: The Maya civilisation lasted over 2,000 years. Tikal had perhaps 60,000 people around 750 CE. Its tallest temple, 65 metres high, appeared in the first Star Wars film.
Spanish conquistadors arrived in 1524 and ruled for nearly 300 years. Guatemala declared independence on 15 September 1821. Torch relay races still celebrate it.
wows: Guatemala has 37 volcanoes, more per square kilometre than almost anywhere.
The ancient Maya made chocolate drinks spiced with chilli.
From Tikal's Temple IV you see only treetops for miles.
The Maya believed a quetzal would die in a cage.
Guatemala City is the biggest city in Central America.
Lake Atitlán is about 340 metres deep.
Guatemala's volcanic soil grows chocolatey coffee.

myths.myth: The Maya predicted the world would end in 2012
myths.fact: That date only ended one long cycle of their calendar. A new cycle began the next day, like a counter rolling back to zero.

myths.myth: Coffee beans grow in pods like peas
myths.fact: Coffee seeds grow inside red fruits called cherries. Farmers pick the cherries and dry them. Then they take out the seeds.
